record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: For an equivariant map Lie algebra M = M(X,g)^Γ, compute the higher Ext groups between finite-dimensional M-modules, explain how these Ext groups interact with both the representation theory of g and the geometry of X, and determine how the global dimension of the category of finite-dimensional M-modules is governed by that geometry.

evidence.quote: (a) Higher extensions. Only the first Ext groups are calculated in [NS], where it is shown that these groups are related to both the representation theory of the target g and the geometry of the scheme X (see, for instance, Proposition 3.5, which involves the tangent space). It is natural to try to compute higher Ext groups. One would expect a rich interplay between these groups and the geometry of the scheme X. It would be particularly interesting to see how the global dimension of the category of finite-dimensional modules is related to this geometry.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over $\mathbb{C}$, let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $\Gamma$ be a finite group acting on both $\mathfrak{g}$ (by Lie algebra automorphisms) and $X$ (by scheme automorphisms). Form the map Lie algebra $M(X,\mathfrak{g}) = \mathfrak{g} \otimes_{\mathbb{C}} \mathcal{O}_X(X)$ with pointwise bracket, and consider its $\Gamma$-fixed-point subalgebra, the equivariant map algebra
$$M = M(X,\mathfrak{g})^{\Gamma} = \{ f \in \mathfrak{g}\otimes\mathcal{O}_X(X) \mid \gamma\cdot f = f \text{ for all } \gamma \in \Gamma\}.$$
Let $\mathcal{F}(M)$ denote the category of finite-dimensional $M$-modules. For finite-dimensional $M$-modules $V$ and $W$ and integers $n \ge 0$, consider the higher extension groups $\mathrm{Ext}^n_M(V,W)$.

(a) Compute $\mathrm{Ext}^n_M(V,W)$ for all $n \ge 0$ in terms of the representation theory of $\mathfrak{g}$ and the geometry (in particular, infinitesimal/local invariants such as tangent spaces and higher cotangent complexes) of the scheme $X$ together with the action of $\Gamma$.

(b) Determine the global dimension of $\mathcal{F}(M)$ and express it in terms of geometric invariants of $X$ (and the action of $\Gamma$ on $X$ and $\mathfrak{g}$).
artifact.status_search_result: First Ext groups between finite-dimensional irreducible modules over equivariant map algebras have been computed (Neher–Savage and follow-ups), and block decompositions and extension results for twisted current algebras have been obtained. However, a general computation of higher Ext^n groups for n ≥ 2 and a determination of the global dimension of the category of finite-dimensional modules in terms of the geometry of X do not appear in the literature, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Extensions and Block Decompositions for Finite-Dimensional Representations of Equivariant Map Algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Describes extensions between irreducible finite-dimensional representations of equivariant map algebras and block decompositions.
status_evidence.claim: First Ext groups and block decompositions have been studied; higher Ext groups and global dimension are not addressed in general.

status_evidence.title: Extensions of modules for twisted current algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Proves that every twisted current algebra is extension-local, removing previous hypotheses on Ext groups.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress concerns Ext^1 and extension-locality, not the full higher Ext computation or global dimension question.
